reason: Same concept (a parameter's default value) spelled two ways inside single documents (js-api.md, cli.md, cpp-api.md, and others). 既定値 is the majority spelling in prose (130 lines / 40 files) and the more formal rendering.

初期値 names a parameter's default on most pages, where 既定値 is canonical. It also correctly names the starting value of an iterative computation, which is a different concept the canonical spelling would be wrong for: the NNDSVD warm start of the NMF, the level smoother's starting point, an early estimate before the stream settles, the tempo tracker's start_bpm prior, and the chain's starting values. Those pages are exempt in full, so a default-sense 初期値 added to one of them will not be caught.

The English form, optionally glossed with the katakana reading on first use, is dominant (133 lines / 42 files) and matches the glossary page title. Several use-cases pages use only the katakana form and never introduce the English term. A first-use reading gloss in the form True Peak（トゥルーピーク）is not a competing spelling and the checker masks it, so a page may introduce the term to a reader meeting it for the first time and use the English form thereafter.

Both render the same referent, and the corpus is not actually split evenly: サンプルレート carries it on 69 lines across 34 files against 6 lines in 4 files. It also matches the katakana reading of the sampleRate field every binding exposes.
192 lines vs 5 for the same referent, with native-synth.md and mixing.md carrying both spellings. Matches the engineering-documentation convention of dropping the terminal long vowel.

Guard entry, not a ban: the two forms name different things and both are correct. Realtime is the proper noun - the subject area's own name in sidebar labels, page titles and the engine and voice-changer features, matching the identifiers. real-time is the ordinary English adjective in front of a common noun (real-time safe, a real-time deadline), and closing it up there is a misspelling rather than a house style. Recorded so the closed form is not banned back onto adjective positions, which is what a substring rule does if it treats them as one term.
Matches the W3C/MDN name and is the form used everywhere else in the corpus (15 lines / 11 files); the closed form appears exactly once.
cli.md uses both spellings for the same referent (the two CLI binaries). Hyphenated is the site's majority form elsewhere in the corpus.
Both forms name the same pipeline stage across files (wasm.md vs introduction.md). Hyphenated matches the sibling term post-processing, which has no closed competitor in this corpus.

Guard entry, not a ban: insertion effect is the correct Roland GS spec term inside GS/EFX documentation. Recorded so a future rule banning it as a variant of the general term insert does not fire on these pages.
